format: Text longer than one line is stored as an array of lines.
scope: offline protocol evidence only; no runtime request, no database

readFrom: the code at staging 2eb786f2 and the R3 card as rendered (task-data/r3/step3/11-card.png and .pdf);
nothing was requested from a runtime or a database

verification.question: Can a wording change break a card that exists?
answer: No. None of the six checks projects facts or draws a PDF. Each compares stored things with stored
things, so the task proceeds and the verification code is not touched.

card_body: The stored body with itself: it parses with UspPropertyCardSchema, the fingerprint of the body without
cardSha256 equals the stored cardSha256, previousRevision follows revision, and resolverUrl names this
stored_linkage: The row columns with the stored body: object_key and artifact_hash name the cardId, revision and
revision_chain: Every earlier row of the card: its body by the card_body rule, its columns by the stored_linkage rule,
and the same plan, packet and target pin as this body (card-verification.ts:95-116). Facts are not
artifact_bytes: The stored PDF bytes with the stored receipt: length and SHA-256 equal artifact.bytes and
artifact.sha256 of the body (card-service.ts:250-256). The PDF is read, never drawn again.
plan_link: The stored body with the stored plan, confirmation and execution: ids, hashes, target, scope, creator,
entry hashes and omissions (card-service.ts:141-150), and those rows with the plan view (:127-140).
packet_bytes: The linked packet through its own reader: the stored packet bytes with the stored packet receipt

whereProjectionAndRenderRun: projectCardFactsTx and renderPropertyCardProfile are called only by generatePropertyCard
(card-service.ts:193, :210), after the replay branch (:167-173) has returned a stored card as it is. The
read, the resolver and the verification call neither.
theLiveCard: Revision 1 of 6a997624-6c8d-40a9-8215-8a671a74dc1c holds its facts as text in its body and its PDF under
its hash. It stays consistent whatever a later projection or renderer writes.
versioning: Not needed for verification. The body stores profile, which names the script coverage of the renderer
and not its words: after this change two cards of one profile can print different words, each exactly as
its own body and bytes state. A wording version would be a new body field in the contract, which this
aNewRevisionOfAnOldCard: A revision appended to an old card is projected and drawn again, so revision 2 prints the new words

stateWord: No row text holds it. The projection stores fact.state (available, unavailable, not_assessed) and both
renderers print it raw in front of the value: card-render.ts:29, card-render-unicode.ts:93.
whatEachRowIsReadFrom.label: Every label is a fixed string at the line named for its row.

rows.label: Selected record
rows.value: read: the plan target label, the kind of the captured record, the pinned revision

rows.label: Registry identifier
rows.value: read: identifier of the captured record (a fixed sentence at :38 when it has none)

rows.label: Application identity
value: read: projectIdentity.code and .status, printed raw (assigned, retired, cancelled_error); "(P3/1)" is

rows.label: Recorded location
value: derived: verticalLocator over projectIdentity.location.locator with the anchor forced to not_supplied
and the parcels dropped, so the row prints NO-ANCHOR on every card. "?" and "L?" are the stored values
of an unknown kind and level

rows.label: Parent parcel assertions
value: read when a selected text entry holds the parcel literal (literal, review state and issuer state, raw;
never on a PDF plan, :50); otherwise a fixed sentence and the anchor state read raw

rows.label: Recorded declared share
value: read from a shared declaration on a text plan (share literal, allocation subject and basis raw, then the
fixed words "technically_accepted; legal not_assessed"); otherwise a fixed sentence

rows.label: Space label (source literal)
rows.value: read: name of the space; then the fixed words "officer-entered, not a boundary"

rows.label: Floor label (source literal)
rows.value: read: name of the parent floor; then fixed words

rows.label: Source citation
rows.value: read: page, region, source id, source revision and source hash of sourceOnly.evidence

rows.label: Geometry / frame / datum
rows.value: fixed sentence, one of two by the kind of plan; state unavailable

aroundTheRows: Heading, footer and the two lines under the QR are fixed sentences written twice, once in each renderer

field: sourceOnly.decision.actor of the source-stated record, beside decision.reason and decision.time
whatTheCommandWrites: POST /api/v1/buildings/{buildingId}/source-spaces runs commandSourceSpace, which sets actor to
localOperatorSubject() (officer/source-spaces.ts:106, :88): the configured local operator subject, which
is process attribution and does not identify a person (usp/principal.ts:22-31). It is a subject id only.
role: None is recorded. The record schema is strict and has no role field; the roles of the request principal
(operator in the local context, principal.ts:35) are not written to the record.
theWordOfficer: sourceOnly.transcription is the literal officer_entered on every source-stated record (schema :35,
writer usp/ingestion/source-building-children.ts:25). It is a fixed word of the record version, says the
label was typed in from the cited region, and cannot tell an officer from another operator.
withoutANewQuery: Yes. card-source-facts.ts:24 already parses the captured target with SourceStatedRecordSchema, so
decision: The record cannot state an officer role, so no wording path prints "officer". The row reads: the label,
"entered by the recording operator from the cited source region; not a boundary".
The subject id is not printed: the card prints no subject today and none was asked for.
The test the task names for an officer-role actor therefore proves the other half: the row names no
officer, and a guard fails when the decision of the record gains a field the wording does not read.

builtFrom: propertyCardResolverUrl (card-render.ts:6-11) with the API_PORT setting, 3188 when unset; the demo
profile expects 3194 (scripts/platform/demo-config.mjs:255). The string is stored in the body, and the
card_body check requires host 127.0.0.1 and this card and revision in the path.
whatAnswers: GET on that path is the resolver (apps/api evidence/property-card.controller.ts:60-81): the stored
one-page PDF of exactly that revision, inline, under the local operator context. 403 once the card is
expired (a card lives at most 24 hours, card-service.ts:174-175) or revoked; 404 for an unknown
revision. The verification read is another route (the same path with /verification).
aPhoneOnAnotherMachine: Gets nothing. 127.0.0.1 is the phone itself, so the request never leaves it and no card data is sent
anywhere. With the host rewritten to the address of the operator machine the API still refuses a host
that is not loopback (403, apps/api common/request-context.ts:64-77).
qr.reportOnly: Making the link reachable from another device is a deployment decision and is not made here.
qr.theRendererHasTheString: Yes, both renderers hold card.resolverUrl, so it can be printed under the QR.
